principles.text: Lower your resting heart rate before bed. It is the single best lever because it drives sleep, willpower, exercise and eating.
Make sleep your #1 priority: same bedtime within ±30 min, screens off 60 min before bed, final food 4 hours before.
Exercise is non-negotiable: about 6 hours a week mixing strength, zone 2, high-intensity cardio, mobility and balance.
Every calorie must fight for its life. Follow evidence, not diet camps, and set firm rules: none is easier than some.
Don't trust labels or anecdotes, only data: measure first and cut any intervention that doesn't move the markers.

sampleQA.question: How do I improve my sleep?

answer.text: Lower your resting heart rate before bed. He calls it the highest-value biomarker you can track daily.
Finish food at least 4 hours before bed. His final meal is around noon, which he calls the single most impactful change he made.
Screens off 60 minutes before bed, a 30-60 minute wind-down, and red or amber light in the evening.
Go to bed within +/- 30 minutes of the same time every night. Inconsistent sleep is as bad as little sleep.

sampleQA.question: How much should I exercise for longevity?

answer.text: About 6 hours a week: 3 strength and 3 cardio sessions, plus flexibility and balance work.
Aim for 150 minutes of zone 2 and 75 minutes of high-intensity cardio weekly, such as the Norwegian 4x4 for VO2 max.
Strength train at least 3x a week with compound push, pull and squat movements and progressive overload.
Do strenuous training at least 4 hours, ideally 6, before bed so it doesn't hurt sleep.

sampleQA.question: Which therapies and supplements are actually worth it?

answer.text: Most wellness tactics don't work. Save time and money and change behavior first, like stopping the one bad habit.
Dry sauna, 15-20 min, 3-7x a week at 80-100°C, is one of his most effective protocols. Men should ice the testicles.
Extra virgin olive oil, 15 ml with every meal, from a lab-tested source.
He stopped rapamycin after almost 5 years because side effects like lipid and glucose changes outweighed the benefits.
